chunks: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and with him was a group of his followers, and the mention of intellect and ignorance came up. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Recognise the intellect and its army, and the ignorance and its army, and you will be rightly guided.' Sama'a said: 'So I said: May I be sacrificed for you! We do not recognise anything except what you have taught us.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the intellect, and it was the first creation from among the spiritual beings, from the right side of the Throne, from His Light. So He said to it: "Turn away!" So it turned away. Then He said to it: "Come forward!" So it came forward. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "I have created you as a magnificent creation, and I have honoured you above all of My creation."'

He said: Then He created ignorance from the bitter, dark ocean. So He said to it: "Turn away!" So it turned away. Then He said to it: "Come forward!" But it did not come forward. So He said to it: "You have been arrogant." So He cursed it. Then He made seventy-five armies for the intellect. So when ignorance saw what Allah had honoured the intellect with and what He had granted it, it harboured enmity towards it. So ignorance said: "O Lord! This is a creation like me. You created it and honoured it and strengthened it, and I am its opposite, and I have no power against it. So grant me an army like what You granted it." So He said: "Yes, but if you disobey after this, I shall expel you and your army from My mercy." It said: "I am satisfied." Then He granted it seventy-five armies.

So from what He gave the intellect from among the seventy-five soldiers: Goodness — and it is the minister of the intellect — and He made its opposite evil — and it is the minister of ignorance. Faith and its opposite is disbelief. Affirmation and its opposite is denial. Hope and its opposite is despair. Justice and its opposite is injustice. Contentment and its opposite is displeasure. Gratitude and its opposite is ingratitude. Aspiration and its opposite is hopelessness. Reliance [on God] and its opposite is greed. Compassion and its opposite is cruelty. Mercy and its opposite is anger. Knowledge and its opposite is ignorance. Understanding and its opposite is foolishness. Chastity and its opposite is shamelessness. Asceticism and its opposite is worldly desire. Gentleness and its opposite is crudeness. Awe [of God] and its opposite is audacity. Humility and its opposite is arrogance. Deliberateness and its opposite is hastiness. Forbearance and its opposite is foolish impulsiveness. Silence and its opposite is blathering. Submission and its opposite is haughtiness. Acceptance and its opposite is doubt. Patience and its opposite is anxiety. Forgiveness and its opposite is revenge. Self-sufficiency and its opposite is poverty. Remembrance and its opposite is heedlessness. Memorization and its opposite is forgetfulness. Kindness and its opposite is severing ties. Contentment and its opposite is covetousness. Consolation and its opposite is withholding.

Cordiality and its opposite is enmity. Faithfulness and its opposite is treachery. Obedience and its opposite is disobedience. Humbleness and its opposite is insolence. Well-being and its opposite is affliction. Love and its opposite is hatred. Truthfulness and its opposite is lying. Truth and its opposite is falsehood. Trustworthiness and its opposite is treachery. Sincerity and its opposite is adulteration. Alertness and its opposite is dullness. Comprehension and its opposite is obtuseness. Recognition and its opposite is denial. Diplomacy and its opposite is exposure. Guarding the unseen and its opposite is scheming. Discretion and its opposite is disclosure. Prayer and its opposite is neglect. Fasting and its opposite is breaking the fast. Struggle and its opposite is cowardice. Pilgrimage and its opposite is breaking the covenant. Guarding speech and its opposite is tale-bearing. Honoring parents and its opposite is disobedience to parents. Sincerity and its opposite is showing off. Good deeds and their opposite is evil deeds. Modesty and its opposite is display. Prudent concealment and its opposite is broadcasting. Fairness and its opposite is bigotry. Preparedness and its opposite is transgression. Cleanliness and its opposite is filth. Modesty and its opposite is impudence. Moderation and its opposite is aggression. Comfort and its opposite is fatigue. Ease and its opposite is difficulty. Blessing and its opposite is diminishment. Well-being and its opposite is calamity. Moderation in living and its opposite is excess. Wisdom and its opposite is caprice. Dignity and its opposite is levity. Happiness and its opposite is wretchedness. Repentance and its opposite is persistence in sin. Seeking forgiveness and its opposite is self-deception. Vigilance and its opposite is negligence. Supplication and its opposite is disdain. Vitality and its opposite is laziness. Joy and its opposite is sorrow. Familiarity and its opposite is separation. And generosity and its opposite is stinginess.

These traits, all of them from the armies of the intellect, are not gathered together except in a prophet, or a successor of a prophet, or a believer whose heart Allah has tested for faith. As for the rest of our followers, none of them is free from having some of these soldiers [of ignorance] until he completes [his faith] and is purified from the soldiers of ignorance. At that point, he will be in the highest rank with the prophets and the successors. And indeed, that is only attained by knowing the intellect and its soldiers, and by avoiding ignorance and its soldiers. May Allah grant us and you success in His obedience and His pleasure.
ai.seo_question: What are the seventy-five armies of intellect and ignorance according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This is one of the most celebrated hadiths in al-Kafi, known as the 'Hadith of the Armies of Intellect and Ignorance.' Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was addressing his close followers when the discussion of intellect and ignorance arose. He taught them that Allah created the intellect as the first spiritual creation from His Light, honoring it above all else, while ignorance was created from a dark bitter ocean and was cursed for its arrogance. Each was given seventy-five armies — paired virtues and vices — ranging from faith vs. disbelief to generosity vs. stinginess. The Imam concluded that only Prophets, their successors, or believers tested by Allah possess all seventy-five virtues, while ordinary followers gradually acquire them through self-purification.
